The moment you eat them, your body converts them into glycidol — classified as a probable human carcinogen by the EPA. Consumer Reports tested 21 popular snacks. The contaminant: glycidyl esters — process chemicals that form when vegetable oils are refined at extreme heat. The moment you eat them, your body converts them into glycidol — classified as a probable human carcinogen by the EPA. Consumer Reports tested 21 popular snacks. Takis had the highest levels. 3.41 micrograms per serving. Nobody else came close.
